transcript:
Meeting header: 
Date: 2026-10-11 16:00 PDT; Duration: ~46m; Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Laura Patel (Silverpine Head of Cloud), Rajesh Varma (Platform Eng), Emily Soto (Security), Tom Hsu (DevOps)

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick check in, can you see my screen?
00:12 Laura: Yeah, we can, thanks Maya. Quick schedule note: we have 45ish minutes.
00:20 Maya: Perfect. Goal for today: handoff the marketplace/on-prem refarch work and confirm KMS and networking blockers so we can move to UAT. Diego will walk the helm/packaging bits.
00:36 Diego: Hi all. I'll start with the packaging overview. We built a helm operator that runs the inference runtime as a statefulset, with a sidecar for metrics. Important: we expose a control plane port for private deployment.
00:50 Rajesh: When you say control plane port, is that plain HTTP or mTLS?
00:55 Diego: It's mTLS by default in our private bundle, certs via K8s secrets. But in marketplace listing we often accept customers using their own ingress termination. There's a config flag - ingress.
01:10 Emily: For security review, we need the exact ciphers and TLS version. Also details on key lifecycle and KMS.
01:20 Maya: Right, KMS was a big topic in prior calls. Diego, can you summarise how Redwood integrates with external KMS?
01:27 Diego: Sure — two patterns. Envelope encryption where the data keys are wrapped by the external KMS. We have support for AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HashiVault via plugin. For HSMs, we also support PKCS#11, but that's in an opt-in path. Note, the current helm chart has placeholders for kms.type and kms.endpoint.
01:47 Tom: We're using an on-prem Thales HSM. Do you support the Thales client?
01:52 Diego: We do not have a native Thales plugin in the upstream chart yet; we can map it through PKCS#11 if the vendor supplies the library. That will require changes to the init container.
02:06 Emily: That change will need security sign-off; give us the proposed init container and a threat model.
02:15 Maya: Action: Diego to create PR with init container snippet. Good.
02:25 Laura: On networking — we have a strict egress policy, and only specific FQDNs are allowed. How much outbound do you need for the Private control plane?
02:35 Diego: Minimal. For hosted telemetry and license checks we reach out to Redwood endpoints, but you can disable telemetry and run totally offline. The marketplace listing expects a contact point for license activation which can be proxied.
02:50 Rajesh: Offline mode — any differences in KV cache behavior?
02:54 Diego: KV cache remains, but cache-warmup relies on a preloaded checkpoint. We have a cache export/import tool that the SE team will walk you through.
03:08 Maya: On marketplace packaging, there are a few gating items: SSO integration (SAML/SCIM), audit logs, and a security questionnaire. We should map those to Silverpine's controls.
03:22 Emily: We are SOC 2 type II in practice — we'll need to see your SOC report and your audit log retention policy. Also RBAC mapping for our AD groups via SAML.
03:36 Maya: We'll attach the SOC2 and security whitepaper in the followup. Diego, we have to call out retention windows exposed in the helm values.
03:46 Diego: Yes, log retention and telemetry retention are configurable; we default to 90 days. In private deployments you can set retention to 0 to avoid storing telemetry.
04:00 Laura: Marketplace requires a test account flow for billing meter tests — what's Redwood's suggested pattern?
04:06 Maya: For billing verification we provide a sandbox meter endpoint and sample usage CSV. For dedicated and private we instrument token-level usage that can be emitted to your billing stack or our metering service. The marketplace package needs a manifest of metering hooks.
04:23 Rajesh: Does that require outbound webhooks?
04:26 Maya: Only if you choose Redwood's hosted metering sink; otherwise you can push metrics to your internal system using our exporter.
04:34 Tom: For on-prem we prefer push, no inbound connections.
04:38 Diego: Push exporter over Prometheus pushgateway or direct OTLP is supported.
04:45 Maya: Okay moving to the refarch diagram — Diego, can you open the latest diagram?
04:50 Diego: I'm sharing now.
05:02 Diego: So the diagram shows two patterns: VPC peering between customer VPC and Redwood managed VPC for private deployments, and an on-prem connector pattern using site-to-site VPN or private link. For on-prem, we recommend a NATed egress with specific routes to reduce blast radius.
05:24 Laura: Site-to-site VPN is preferred, is there a requirement for BGP?
05:29 Diego: We don't require BGP, static routes are fine for initial pilot, but for scale BGP is more resilient.
05:36 Emily: Any firewall port lists?
05:38 Diego: Yes — control plane: TCP 8443, metrics: TCP 9090, data plane (gRPC) 10080-10090 by default. We'll supply a full proposed firewall matrix.
05:53 Rajesh: Curious about latency — if we go VPC peering vs private link, what's the typical p95 token latency difference?
06:00 Diego: In our internal benchmarks peering gave sub-20ms p95 within-region; private link can add 8–25ms depending on path. But that depends on model size, sequence length, batching.
06:18 Maya: Which brings up quantization/throughput guidance — Diego, we had a note about quantized model variants for cost/perf.
06:25 Diego: Right, we provide float16 and int8 variants. For inference accuracy-sensitive workloads you'd likely choose float16. We can run a small eval on your prompt set in staging to see regression.
06:40 Laura: We'll need that eval before committing to a marketplace SKU.
06:44 Maya: Agreed. We'll schedule a prompt-set eval in staging.
06:49 Tom: About RBAC — mapping to AD groups via SAML; do you support group sync or just group assertions?
06:56 Diego: We support SCIM for user provisioning and group sync, and SAML group assertions for immediate mapping. SCIM requires outbound provisioning to your SCIM endpoint which some customers avoid.
07:08 Emily: So for us, group assertions only, no SCIM.
:07:12 Diego: Noted.
07:15 Maya: Let's surface the marketplace cert gates — can we go through the checklist quickly?
07:20 Laura: Yes please.
07:22 Maya: Items: security questionnaire complete, packaging manifests (helm), RBAC and SSO flow documented, KMS compatibility declared, billing/metering manifest, support SLA, and a customer UAT plan.
07:37 Rajesh: On packaging manifests, do you require a specific helm repo layout?
07:41 Diego: We prefer OCI registry or standard chartmuseum layout. We also ask for a values.schema.json to verify required fields.
07:51 Tom: Does Redwood have an example values.schema.json?
07:54 Diego: Yes, I'll attach a canonical example.
07:58 Maya: Side note — a couple partners have raised concerns about reliant vendor lock-in in marketplace listings; competitors mentioned OctoCloud has a single-tenant-only approach which customers like for isolation. Do you want me to call that out?
08:18 Laura: We are worried about lock-in. How easy is moving state out?
08:22 Diego: We provide state export tools: checkpoint export for models, KV cache dump, and configuration export. We try to make migrations reproducible.
08:32 Emily: For compliance we need an audit of deletion flow — if a tenant requests deletion, what's the guarantee?
08:37 Maya: We have a documented data deletion policy and can provide SLA for deletion in private deployments. We'll attach the policy.
08:45 Rajesh: Regarding observability — how do traces and PII get redacted?
08:50 Diego: We have redaction hooks in the ingestion pipeline; by default we don't capture full prompts in hosted telemetry, but customers can enable locally for debugging.
09:03 Tom: Next, can we discuss the UAT plan? We have a 2-week window in staging and then a rolling canary.
09:12 Maya: Typical plan: week 1 smoke + integration tests (networking, SSO, KMS), week 2 performance validations and billing tests, then a 3-day canary in prod.
09:24 Laura: Sounds good. We'll need a runbook for failover to the previous variant; do you have automatic fallback?
09:31 Diego: Yes, the runtime supports automatic fallback to a smaller model variant on error, and the console has rollout controls to rollback. We'll demonstrate in the canary.
09:43 Emily: Any known gotchas for on-prem?
09:46 Diego: Disk throughput and GPU driver versions are common issues. Also kernel modules for certain HSM clients can be finicky.
09:55 Maya: Ok, we're approaching mid-point. Quick check: who owns the refarch doc updates?
10:01 Diego: SE (me) will iterate, Maya will review for marketplace language.
10:08 Laura: We'll provide network diagrams and KMS vendor contacts by Thursday.
10:12 Maya: Great.
10:15 Diego: I'll also add a sample PKCS#11 snippet referencing the Thales flow; it's not finalized but should help Silverpine's security team review.
10:29 Emily: Please note we need a threat model for the PKCS#11 path.
10:33 Diego: Understood.
10:36 Maya: Anything else on packaging?
10:38 Tom: How do you handle upgrades for statefulsets without losing caches?
10:43 Diego: We use a drain/sync strategy: export KV cache, patch, then warm from checkpoint. For smaller caches we do rolling restart with a shared warmup bucket. We'll put the playbook in the repo.
11:02 Rajesh: Can you clarify the licensing handshake in offline mode? The marketplace listing sometimes enforces online activation.
11:10 Maya: For private/on-prem we support offline license activation via signed token bundles. We'll provide the sample tool to generate and verify tokens.
11:19 Laura: Billing — we need meter samples to validate our internal chargeback.
11:24 Maya: We'll send a sample usage CSV and an endpoint to run meter validation in staging.
11:32 Diego: Quick note about provisioning: helm values include a nodeSelector that we recommend for GPU isolation and a toleration set for NVIDIA drivers. If you need guidance for MPS vs dedicated GPU slicing we'll consult.
11:52 Tom: We currently plan for dedicated GPUs.
11:55 Diego: Good, then we'll include recommended GPU instance types and queue sizes for your expected QPS.
12:06 Maya: Ok time check — 15 minutes left. Let's recap actions and owners.
12:12 Maya: Diego: helm values + PKCS#11 snippet + example values.schema.json by Oct 15.
12:20 Diego: Yep.
12:21 Maya: Maya: send SOC2 + security whitepaper + marketplace manifest template by Oct 13.
12:28 Maya: Laura: network topology + KMS vendor details by Oct 14.
12:33 Laura: We'll do that.
12:36 Emily: We'll review the threat model within 5 business days of receiving the PKCS#11 PR.
12:42 Maya: Final Q — any blockers to UAT scheduling?
12:46 Laura: Only waiting on KMS test credentials and network matrix.
12:50 Maya: Good. We'll follow up with a calendar invite for the UAT kickoff and share a docs link.
12:57 Tom: Thanks everyone.
13:00 Maya: Thanks, bye.

Meeting adjourned.
